To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the oxidation of methionine residues in DHFR was observed during long storage, and that the oxidation of the methionines resulted in the loss of enzyme activity.

(a) the oxidation sites of a stored protein were identified through LC-MS, (b) the enzyme activity of an oxidized protein was not always lower than that of the native protein, (c) a stored protein is not a simple mixture of native and oxidized proteins, and (d) the activity itself is a poor measure for quality control.

the oxidatively modified methionine residues are located in different positions in the DHFR molecule depending on the storage time, and that the oxidation of the methionines in the active center of the enzyme affects its activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oxidation of the protein during storage, and the results obtained provide a useful tool for the quality control of proteins in the pharmaceutical industry.
protein oxidation, which may occur during long storage of a protein.
the identification of the oxidation site of proteins in terms of amino acids through LC-MS studies, and the relationship between the oxidation and enzyme activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the oxidation of the protein is not a simple process, but rather a very complicated one, and that the oxidation of methionine residues, which is one of the major causes for the decrease in enzyme activity, is not necessarily a bad thing for the quality control of the protein, as it can be seen from the fact that one of the methione-sulfoxe DHFRs showed a higher activity.
the oxidation of a protein during storage is not always detrimental, but may be beneficial in some cases.
the oxidation of a single methionine residue in DHFR is not detrimental to the enzyme activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oxidation of methionine residues in proteins is reversible, but the oxidation of cysteine residues is not.

the protein oxidation in a cysteine-deficient protein during storage is not necessarily a simple process, but rather a complex one, which depends on the amino acid sequence, the number of cysteine residues and the number of methionine residues, and that it is important to identify the oxidation site in order to evaluate the quality of the protein.
the oxidation of a single methionine residue, even if it is not a catalytic site, can cause the change in the enzyme activity of DHFR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to identify the oxidation sites of proteins for quality control.
the molecular mass of a protein should be carefully monitored during long-term storage of the protein.
the molecular masses of proteins stored as an ammonium salt precipitate for a long time can be increased by 16 Da due to oxidation of a methionine residue.
